headline: Rivercell, a Paris startup, has launched with $25 million to build AI models that predict how human cells respond to drugs and genetic changes.
score_reason: Early-stage seed launch reported on 7 Oct 2026 with no results yet; lowered by 1 from 5.
importance_line: Adds to the push to predict cell behaviour by computer before lab testing, which drug developers hope will cut costs, but it is a seed-stage company with no results shown.
summary: AllSci reports that Rivercell, a Paris startup, has come out of stealth with a $25 million seed round led by HV to train what it calls an AI Virtual Cell model on large datasets about how single cells respond to drugs and genetic changes, produced in its own automated lab. Its founders include Yann Fleureau, who co-founded the AI diagnostics firm Cardiologs, and Eric Durand, formerly of Novartis and Owkin.
notes: Launch date 7 Oct 2026 from another outlet's listing; AllSci ran it 8 Oct.
